'''Gastón Guzmán Huerta''' (26 August 1932 – 12 January 2016), a Mexican [[mycology|mycologist]] and [[anthropology|anthropologist]], was an authority on the genus ''[[Psilocybe]]''.

==Career==
He was born in [[Xalapa]], [[Veracruz]], in 1932. His interest in [[mycology]] began in 1955 when as a graduate student he decided to update his school's ([[National Polytechnic Institute]]) poorly kept collection of fungi. During his early field work he found a large assortment of species about which little was known at the time. This inspired him to choose fungi as the topic of his professional thesis.<ref name="Dr. Gaston Guzman">{{Cite web|url=http://www.stainblue.com/guzman.htm|title = Dr. Gaston Guzman}}</ref>

In 1957 Guzmán was invited by the University of Mexico to assist [[Rolf Singer]], who would arrive to Mexico the following year to study the hallucinogenic mushroom genus ''Psilocybe''. Guzmán accepted and assisted Singer through his explorations in Mexico. While they were in the [[Huautla de Jiménez]] region, in their last day of the expeditions, they met [[R. Gordon Wasson]]. For Guzmán it was a "fructiferous meeting."<ref name="Guzmán-Dávalos 2005"/>

In 1958, he published his first paper on a blue-staining ''Psilocybe'' species and the first paper on the ecology of neurotropic fungi. In 1971, he received a grant from the [[John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation|Guggenheim Foundation]] of [[New York City]], on the recommendation of [[Richard Evans Schultes]]<ref name="Dr. Gaston Guzman"/> to study the genus ''Psilocybe'', which resulted in a comprehensive [[monograph]] on the subject in 1983, titled ''The Genus Psilocybe: A Systematic Revision of the Known Species Including the History, Distribution and Chemistry of the Hallucinogenic Species''.<ref>The Genus Psilocybe: A Systematic Revision of the Known Species Including the History, Distribution and Chemistry of the Hallucinogenic Species</ref> He also authored eight other books and over 350 papers on Mexican mushrooms and has [[species description|described]] more than 200 new [[taxon|taxa]] of fungi worldwide. More than half of the known [[psilocybin mushroom]] species were first described by Guzmán and his collaborators.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Guzmán |first=Gastón |title=The genus Psilocybe: a systematic revision of the known species including the history, distribution, and chemistry of the hallucinogenic species |date=1983 |publisher=J. Cramer |isbn=978-3-7682-5474-8 |series=Beihefte zur Nova Hedwigia |location=Vaduz [Liechtenstein]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Stamets |first=Paul |title=Psilocybin Mushrooms of the World: An Identification Guide |date=2023 |publisher=Potter/Ten Speed/Harmony/Rodale |others=Andrew Weil |isbn=978-1-60774-199-2 |location=New York}}</ref>

A co-founder and former president of the Mexican Mycological Society (1965), he was also president of the Latin American Mycological Association (2000–2002), founded by him in [[La Habana]], Cuba, in 1990. Guzmán held an emeritus research chair at the Ecological Institute of Xalapa where he founded the Department and Herbarium of Fungi which now has more than 50,000 specimens. In 1955 he founded the Mycological Herbarium at the National School of Biological Sciences (ENCB) in Mexico City. ENCB now has more than 100,000 specimens, the most sizable collection in Mexico.

==Personal life==
Guzmán's daughter, [[Laura Guzmán Dávalos]], is also a prominent mycologist. She founded the Mycology Department at the [[University of Guadalajara]].

Guzmán died of a [[heart attack]] in [[Guadalajara]], Mexico on 12 January 2016, at the age of 83.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.conacyt.mx/index.php/comunicacion/comunicados-prensa/561-el-conacyt-lamenta-el-sensible-fallecimiento-del-dr-gaston-guzman|title=El Conacyt lamenta el sensible fallecimiento del Dr. Gastón Guzmán|publisher=Conacyt.com|access-date=January 16, 2016|language=es}}</ref>

{{botanist|Guzmán}}

==Eponymy==
Several fungus species have been named in Guzmán's honor:
*''Crepidotus guzmanii'' Singer 1973<ref name="Singer 1973b"/>
*''Fistulina guzmanii'' Brusis 1973<ref name="Brusis 1973"/>
*''Marasmiellus guzmanii'' Singer 1973<ref name="Singer 1973b"/>
*''Pseudohiatula guzmaniana'' Singer 1973<ref name="Singer 1973"/>
*''Marasmius guzmanianus'' Singer 1976<ref name="Singer 1976"/>
*''[[Neotremella guzmanii]]'' Lowy 1979<ref name="Lowy 1979"/>
*''Psilocybe guzmanii'' Natarajan & Raman 1983<ref name="Natarajan 1983"/>
*''Amanita guzmanii'' Cifuentes, Villegas & G.Santiago 1984<ref name="Santiago 1984"/>
*''Entoloma guzmanii'' Courtec. 1986<ref name="Courtecuisse 1986"/>
*''[[Antromycopsis guzmanii]]'' Stalpers, Seifert & Samson 1991<ref name="Stalpers 1991"/>
*''Phylloporus guzmanii'' Montoya & Bandala 1991<ref name="Montoya 1991"/>
*''Pseudocyphellaria guzmanii'' D.J.Galloway 1992<ref name="Galloway 1992"/>
*''Rhizopogon guzmanii'' Trappe & Cázares 1992<ref name="Cazares 1992"/>
*''Camillea guzmanii'' F.San Martín & J.D.Rogers 1993<ref name="San Martín 1993"/>
*''Coralloderma guzmanii'' A.L.Welden 1993<ref name="Welden 1993"/>
*''Phaeocollybia guzmanii'' Bandala & Montoya 1994<ref name="Bandala-Muñoz 1994"/>
*''Suillus guzmanii'' G.Moreno, Bandala & Montoya 1997<ref name="Moreno 1997"/>
*''Tuber guzmanii'' Trappe & Cázares 2006
*''Calvatia guzmanii'' C.R.Alves & Cortez 2012<ref name="Alves 2013"/>
*''[[Cora guzmaniana]]'' Moncada, R.-E.Pérez & Lücking 2019<ref name="Moncada et al. 2019"/>
